# dsh-550c-monitor
A system monitor for the DSH Web UI, cut to match the **550C** skin: a translucent instrument panel
that docks to the right edge of the reading column and reads CPU, GPU, memory, disk, network and tem
he right edge of the reading column and reads CPU, GPU, memory, disk, network and temperatures live.
It is a companion plugin to `dsh-550c-skin` — but it also runs on its own, falling back to the host
theme tokens when the skin is not installed.
[代码示例省略，未执行]
## Features

**Six live readings**
- **CPU** — total load from `os.cpus()` tick deltas, plus core count.
- **GPU*

* — utilisation and memory used when `nvidia-smi` is present; silently absent otherwise.
- **MEM** —

used / total physical memory.
- **DSK** — free space on the volume that holds `$DSH_HOME`, with the

mount point.
- **NET** — receive / transmit throughput, sampled per interval (no counters → no numb

er: it shows `--` for the first ~4 s instead of inventing `0`).
- **TMP** — GPU temperature from `nv
idia-smi`, CPU temperature from the ACPI thermal zone when the process is allowed to read it.
**A device ledger** — host, OS, CPU model, memory, GPU, disk volume, LAN address, Node version, scre
en, time zone. On short windows the optional rows fold away from the bottom up, so the numbers are n
ever clipped mid-line.

**Built like the skin**
- Square instrument rails: 4 px cells on a 6 px pitch, `skewX(-18deg)`, fill
in the accent colour, a 1 px liquid-level line overhanging both edges, and a hard square corner (no

blurred dropshadow — it rounds 4 px cells into pills).
- Frosted glass card: translucent tint over
`backdrop-filter: blur(34px) saturate(1.32)`, a 5 %→1 % top highlight, faint scan lines, and four co

rner brackets drawn from eight gradients.
- HUD numerals: tabular, slashed-zero, `text-shadow` bloom

; labels carry a 2×10 px status tick.
- Palette first reads the skin's tokens (`--c-amber`, `--c-glo
w-rgb`, `--c-red`, `--c-text-*`), then the host theme (`--dsw-alias-*`) as a fallback.

**Behaves like an instrument, not a dialog**
- **Drag it** by the title bar; double-click the title

bar to hand it back to the layout engine. The position survives reloads.
- **Fold it** with the `–`
/ `+` key at the top right — one 46 px strip showing `CPU · MEM · NET`. The fold state survives relo

ads.
- **Adapts**: the panel targets the right gutter of the reading column, capped at 60 % of the v
isible height so the bottom-right corner stays free for other widgets. Narrow windows collapse it to

an 18 px rail of six thin bars.
- Click-through everywhere except the title bar and the fold key; i
t hides itself while a dialog or menu is open.

**Widens the reading column** (opt-in default: on)
DSH clamps the transcript to a reading measure, w
hich leaves a wide empty gutter on a large screen. This plugin finds the box that is *actually* clam
ped by `max-width` (computed limit in px, and the box already touching it), marks that single elemen
t with `data-550c-monitor-wide`, and drops the clamp. Nothing else is touched; the pass is throttled
to once every 3 s and is fully reversible from the console:
[代码示例省略，未执行]
The choice is remembered in `localStorage` (`dsh-550c-monitor:wide`).
## Requirements

- DSH Web UI with a Web server (the plugin registers one exact route).
- Node.js **>= 20**.
- Window
s or Linux for the system probes; Windows additionally gives CPU temperature (when elevated) and GPU
readings via `nvidia-smi`. macOS is untested.
## Install
From a local checkout (the plugin is plain JS — no build step):

then enable the bundle for the profile (`dsh.profile.bundles` in the profile's `package.json`), or u
se the Harness plugin manager UI. The package declares its own `dsh.bundle.patch`, so nothing has to
be hand-written into `cordis.patch.yml`.
The row lands in the profile as `monitor-550c`.

## Notes on the numbers
- **CPU temperature** comes from `MSAcpi_ThermalZoneTemperature`. Reading it needs an elevated proce
ss on most laptops; when the probe is refused (or the machine exposes no ACPI thermal zone — most de
sktops don't), the row shows `GPU`'s value only and `TMP` falls back to reporting the GPU sensor. Th

e probe gives up after two consecutive refusals instead of polling forever.
- **Networking** is read
from `netstat -e` on Windows and `/proc/net/dev` on Linux. If neither answers, the rows show `--`.
- **GPU** is polled with a one-shot `nvidia-smi` query per interval; when the binary is missing the

GPU row is omitted and the remaining rows keep the panel's rhythm.
- **Disk** is the volume holding

`$DSH_HOME` (falls back to the user's home volume).
- Host-side probing is done with `spawn` writing
to a scratch file rather than piped stdio, because some sandboxes refuse anonymous pipes (`spawn EP
scratch file rather than piped stdio, because some sandboxes refuse anonymous pipes (`spawn EPERM`).
## Development
[代码示例省略，未执行]
The client half is intentionally written as a hand-rolled module — DSH loads it as-is. It appends on
e `<style>` element and one `position: fixed` card to the document, both owned by a single cleanup f
unction registered through `ctx.effect`.
